thread:
maria: Heads-up, p50 latency up ~8% on small-seq workloads after yesterday's kernel reorder. Seen in staging and a few canaries.
kevin: ugh. which change specifically? the kernel selection priority or the attention path tweak?
maria: kernel priority reorder + added a fallback that prefers the 'hybrid' kernel for seq<=64. hypothesis: hybrid has worse steady-state batching for mixed lengths — it blocks longer while waiting for short seqs to hit token budget.
oliver: do we have trace of batch formation? I want to see queue hold times and token_budget consumption per batch.
maria: yes, attaching quick paste from trace: ```
queue_events: [wait_ms: 12, 45, 120, 7, 300]
batches: [{size:3, tokens:18, kernel:hybrid, start_wait:120}, {size:12, tokens:240, kernel:optimized-attn, start_wait:7}]
```
samira: that 120ms wait for tiny 18-token batch is the killer. looks like token_budget_target is set too low for hybrid path or hybrid isn't compatible with the continuous batching fast-path so requests get gated.
kevin: could be interaction with paged-KV allocation too — hybrid currently pins paged-kv slots eagerly which causes enqueueing to stall until KV metadata is ready. for small seq that's overhead.
perf-bot: nightly-regression: small-seq-p50 +8.2% (ci/staging), cpu spin +5%, gpu occupancy -6% after commit 3f2a1b. See /artifacts/perf/177200/ for profiles.
maria: core ask: revert kernel priority to previous ordering for canaries and experiment with increasing token_budget_target from 64->128 for hybrid-only flows. also add metric for "kernel_block_wait_ms" per request.
oliver: alternative: keep hybrid fallback but change queue policy to opportunistic: if head request waiting > X ms, flush with whatever accumulated and mark kernel as incompatible for subsequent similar-length requests for short window. that reduces pathological waits.
kevin: agree. implement two quick knobs: token_budget_target and opportunistic_flush_ms. default opportunistic_flush_ms=50ms, token_budget_target=128 for hybrid.
samira: also let's add a guard: if kernel_pref==hybrid and queued_tokens < min_tokens_for_hybrid then prefer optimized-attn. avoids hybrid trying to service tiny batches.
maria: sounds good. I'll put up a small PR with config defaults + perf logging. @kevin can you add a micro-benchmark to simulate mixed-length Poisson arrivals (p=0.7 long, 0.3 short) so we can measure batching under both kernel orders?
kevin: on it. will create synthetic load with arrival profile and KV allocation latencies.
perf-bot: perf-test queued: run 177201 - mixed-poisson. baseline vs hybrid-priority. artifacts will show batch sizes, wait_ms distribution, kernel_switch_count.
maria: thanks. if numbers look good we'll roll to a subset of canaries. for rollback plan: revert commit or flip kernel_priority feature flag.
oliver: one more note: ensure kernel telemetry includes "attempted_prefetch_pagedkv" boolean so we can correlate paged-kv stalls to queue waits.
samira: added to the checklist. also add a quick A/B in dedicated pool to ensure no regressions under sustained load.
maria: ok pushing PR now. will tag reviewers. :rocket: 
kevin: thx, will have bench results in ~45m.
perf-bot: alert: canary cluster 3 observed slight token-eviction spikes; investigating TTL interactions.
maria: noted. let's hold canary rollout until bench + KV guard in.
kevin: ack.
